selection.rationale: Selected boundary: group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f is the decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM module forward, a single observed call (323bcbe006b343648b346af9, 31 invocations per run, signature {input_ids[1,1] int64 cuda, past_key_values: DynamicCache, use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1}); it is the sole editable parent of every decode-phase kernel site and the only boundary where per-step host dispatch can be removed without touching the frozen adapter loop or the phase-guarded prefill path (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f stays parent, TTFT untouched). Why this opportunity: measured baseline is 40.01 tok/s with decode_ms 771.96 of 799.57 end-to-end (96.5% of the objective window) while this group's diagnostic CUDA is only 374.19ms, i.e. ~12.07ms/step of kernels vs ~24.9ms/step wall; execution_timeline shows 66,441 kernels with only 386.0ms active union against 1,073.5ms of inter-kernel gaps in the (perturbed) 1,459.5ms profiled span; device_telemetry shows 58% GPU and 46-47% memory-bandwidth utilization during decode; python_runtime's perturbed cProfile counts 17,472 nn.Module _call_impl dispatches per run. The workload is launch/host-bound, not kernel-bound, so no single faster kernel moves the metric - removing per-step Python dispatch and launch gaps across this whole boundary is the remaining lever. Why a re-selection rather than a new family: the previous trial at this exact boundary (trial-5af74ce3b2, inspected in inputs/previous-candidate/) was rejected solely on quality, with coverage proving its graph path executed (routes captured:1, reseeded:1, replay:62, no fallbacks) and a deterministic logits failure in both continuous steps: 1,131,606/4,861,952 elements (23.3%) beyond atol 0.02/rtol 0.02, max abs error 1.0 first at (0,6,50898), identical signature in both repeats. Measured fact: divergence on the replay path, deterministic, mid-sequence. Failure cause (hypothesis grounded in the worker's transformers 5.16.1 source): the captured graph swapped the parent's eager attention dispatch - with DynamicCache, q_len==1 and no padding, masking_utils.py:952 keeps allow_is_causal_skip true so sdpa runs with attn_mask=None and enable_gqa=True over exactly-length concatenated KV - for the StaticCache compileable-cache path, where the same rule disables the skip, materializes an explicit bool mask, and sdpa_attention.py then repeat_kv-expands the full-width 288-slot static K/V (use_gqa_in_sdpa requires attn_mask None); the masked/expanded kernel reorders bf16 reductions enough to flip a near-tie greedy argmax (require_exact_greedy_tokens), after which the continuation legitimately diverges with O(1) logit errors concentrated from roughly step 6 onward. The prior CPU-only equivalence check could not observe this because both paths share the math backend on CPU. Repair direction for the next candidate at this boundary: the replayed work must be the eager parent's exact kernel sequence - capture per-step-position CUDA graphs (one per decode step index r=0..30, KV length 257..287, fixed per-graph positions/lengths that are each correct only for their step) from the parent forward while it executes its eager DynamicCache-style path (mask skipped, enable_gqa, exact-length cat slices over a static KV arena with a shared graph pool), reseeded from each run's prefill DynamicCache via per-run cache-identity detection, with the previous trial's labeled signature/structure/setup/runtime fallbacks to the parent reference unchanged. State semantics stay as before: per-run reseed keeps the workload on current inputs, the incoming DynamicCache is returned unmutated, and one-time capture lands outside measured repeats. Scope is 'group' with exactly this group's call as affected_calls; the inner aten/module sites of the decode phase are affected only in that they stop Python-dispatching during replay while their native kernels still execute inside the graph, which the proposal stage should declare as before.
selection.hypothesis: If per-decode-step CUDA graphs captured from the parent's own eager kernel sequence (attn_mask skipped with enable_gqa over exact-length KV slices, identical aten op order) replace the 31 decode invocations of call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, then logits are reproduced kernel-for-kernel (bit-identical modulo per-graph address changes), exact greedy tokens are preserved, and decode wall falls from ~24.9ms/step toward the ~12.1ms/step kernel floor plus small copy/clone/replay overhead - decode_ms from ~772ms to roughly 390-450ms and generated_tokens_per_second from the measured 40.0 toward ~65-75 tok/s - because the removed ~12.8ms/step of host dispatch and launch gaps (1,073.5ms of kernel gaps in the profiled window) is the dominant, measured cost; the previous StaticCache-path failure is expected to disappear because the repair eliminates the only measured divergence source (masked repeat_kv SDPA dispatch over full-width buffers) rather than tolerating it within tolerance. This is a paired-measurement hypothesis, not an acceptance claim: if capture of the exact eager sequence is infeasible or quality still diverges, the labeled fallback preserves parent semantics and the metric reverts to baseline.

proposal.rationale: Selected boundary: group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f is the decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM forward (call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, 31 invocations per run, sole member). The measured baseline (project.json) attributes 771.96ms of the 799.57ms end-to-end wall to decode versus 27.66ms TTFT, and target-resources/call-resources evidence shows the decode call's diagnostic CUDA time is only 374.19ms (~12.07ms/step of kernels against ~24.9ms/step wall): roughly half of every step is host dispatch and inter-kernel idle across ~2,073 tiny kernels per step (64,263 total, ~5.8us average) that already run near memory bandwidth. Removing per-step host dispatch is therefore the only lever that moves generated_tokens_per_second. Repair of the previous failed attempt (trial-5af74ce3b2, decision no_valid_parameter_candidate): its CUDA graph replayed a StaticCache forward, which on this transformers 5.16.1 stack takes a numerically different branch than the parent DynamicCache path the reference observation is generated from - StaticLayer.get_mask_sizes returns max_cache_len, so decode materializes a 288-wide masked SDPA with is_compileable caches, while the DynamicCache path skips the causal mask and runs exact-length unmasked SDPA with enable_gqa. Different reduction shapes in bf16 drift, compound autoregressively, and exceeded the 0.02 tolerances from generation row 6 (23.3% mismatched logits, max abs 1.0, identical deterministic failure on both continuous steps), consistent with a numerics-path divergence rather than missing work (coverage showed 62 replays plus capture and reseed). This candidate keeps the graph idea but makes replay numerically exact by construction and verified at runtime: (1) a cache facade (CacheLayerMixin subclass) writes K/V in place into fixed-width static buffers and returns exact-length slices [:, :, :L+1] with is_compileable=False, so the model's mask logic, SDPA enable_gqa dispatch, kernel shapes and input values are exactly the DynamicCache decode path - verified bit-identical (max|d|=0.0, equal greedy tokens) against the parent path in fp32 and bf16 on CPU with the worker's transformers/torch; (2) on the first decode call of the first run, the true parent greedy chain is computed eagerly through context.references on a value-identical cloned DynamicCache (the run's real cache is never mutated) - this is both the acceptance reference and the warmup covering every per-step kernel shape; (3) the full 31-step decode loop (embedding lookup, forward, argmax token chain, per-step KV writes at baked positions prompt_len+s) is then captured in ONE torch.cuda.CUDAGraph through context.references inside the adapter's decode phase, replayed once, and must reproduce the true chain's logits (allclose atol=rtol=0.01, half the frozen tolerance) and its exact greedy token chain before it is ever served; (4) each subsequent run reseeds the static buffers from that run's actual prefill DynamicCache (~37MB D2D, ~1-2ms) plus the run's step-0 token, replays once, and serves per-step logits clones at the 31 observed call boundaries, so every invocation executes the workload on its current inputs (no fixture data is baked into the graph; tokens/logits/KV are recomputed per replay). Expected effect: decode wall falls from ~772ms toward the ~374ms kernel floor plus seeding/replay overhead (~380-400ms), end-to-end ~410-430ms, raising generated_tokens_per_second from the measured 40.0 toward ~75-78 (paired repeats will decide). Any facade mismatch, graph divergence, unsupported signature, setup exception or replay runtime failure routes to fallback:setup-failure/fallback:runtime-failure labels and serves the verified eager chain or the plain parent reference, so quality degrades to baseline behavior, never to unverified outputs. The prefill group stays on the parent path via the framework's phase guard, leaving TTFT untouched; state/reset semantics are preserved because the run's DynamicCache is returned unchanged and each run's graph state is rebuilt from that run's prefill cache.

setup_work.when: inside the first decode-phase invocation (adapter quality/warmup runs); scored repeats only pay per-run reseed+replay
actions: allocate fixed-width static K/V buffers for 36 layers (2 x [1,8,287,128] bf16 per layer, about 42.4MB total) plus a [1,1] int64 step-0 token buffer
seed static buffers from the run's prefill DynamicCache (D2D copy, per run, ~1-2ms)
run the true eager parent greedy chain through context.references on a value-identical cloned DynamicCache (31 steps, side stream, also warms every kernel shape; the real cache is never mutated)

capture one CUDA graph unrolling all 31 decode steps through context.references over the facade, replay it once and gate it against the true chain (logits allclose 0.01/0.01 and exact greedy token equality)
per subsequent run: reseed, replay once, clone the 31 logits tensors
setup_work.memory: retained after setup: ~42.4MB static K/V buffers, graph private pool holding the unrolled intermediates and 31 logits outputs (~10-25MB expected, exact size observed at runtime), ~9.2MB transient per-run logits clones, and a ~38MB transient clone-cache seed during first-run validation (returned to the caching allocator afterwards). Baseline peak_allocated is ~8.18GB, so setup adds well under 1%; framework.peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle peaks may rise slightly - no memory saving is claimed.

quality_risks: graph-vs-eager equivalence is gated at runtime: the replayed graph must reproduce the true parent chain's logits (atol=rtol=0.01, half the frozen quality tolerance) and its exact greedy token chain; on any mismatch the graph is discarded and the verified eager chain or plain parent reference is served, so the route degrades to baseline speed with parent-exact outputs

the facade's exact-length slice/mask-skip path was verified bit-identical to the DynamicCache parent path on CPU (fp32 and bf16) on the worker's transformers 5.16.1/torch 2.13; the GPU-side gate additionally requires a one-step eager facade probe to match the true chain before capture is attempted

the graph bakes the frozen decode geometry (batch 1, 256 prompt positions, 31 steps, bf16, observed kwarg signature); calls with any other signature, shape, dtype, device or training mode fall back to the parent reference, and a run whose prefill cache length differs from the captured one uses the plain parent path

CUDA-graph replay does not re-run Python hooks; runtime coverage is preserved because all 31 observed call boundaries still invoke the replacement, which returns each step's verified logits, and the validation chain itself invokes context.references 32 times on real shapes

deterministic-kernel assumption: replay executes the kernels captured from the eager parent sequence; the acceptance gate compares against the eager chain run in the same process on the same device, and cuBLAS/cuDNN run-to-run nondeterminism (if any) would surface as a validation failure and fall back rather than a silent quality regression

retained graph pool and static buffers add roughly 55-75MB to lifecycle memory; peak_allocated during the first (warmup/quality) invocation includes the transient validation clone (~38MB); neither counter decrease nor physical-memory saving is claimed
